rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse seems vague about which term Moses fulfilled, Elmalılı infers he completed more than required and had no term left; a noble person keeps his promise.
rows.anchor: düşünülünce fazlasını ödediği ve hiçbir eceli kalmadığı anlaşılır. Çünkü kerîm olan vaadine vefâ eder

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some reports say Moses remained ten years beyond the agreed period.
rows.anchor: Hatta bazılarında on sene daha fazla kaldığı rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some say Moses was heading to Egypt, though Elmalılı considers this at odds with his earlier fear that they would kill him.
rows.anchor: bazıları Mısır’a demişler lâkin فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ demesi buna münâfî görünür

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Others say he headed toward Jerusalem; Elmalılı finds this safer and more apt.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da Kudüs’e doğru demişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says ānasa conveys a deep, humanly intimate perception rather than crude sensing; he compares its use for recognizing maturity in 4:6.
rows.anchor: bir ihsas ifade etmekle beraber, kaba bir ihsâsın değil, üns ifade eden derin ve insânî bir ihsâsın ifadesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite tanwin on nāran carries further strange and wondrous implications.
rows.anchor: نَارًۭا’daki tenvînin tenkîrindeki garâib ve acâiblik de öyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's hope of bringing news suggests the travelers were in a difficult situation and needed information on the road.
rows.anchor: demek ki yolda bir haber almaya muhtaç sıkıntılı bir vaziyette bulunuyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account places the family traveling in winter through unfamiliar routes, with Moses avoiding Syrian rulers; his pregnant wife and party reached Sinai's right or western side on a dark, cold, snowy night.
rows.anchor: Kış mevsimi ehliyle, malıyla çıkmış ve Şam mülûkünden hazeren yolun gayrısını tutmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Moses traveled at night to rejoin his companions, lost the way, and his wife went into labor; when his flint failed, he saw a distant fire and told them to wait.
rows.anchor: Haremine gayretinden geceleyin refikleriyle buluşur, gündüz ayrılırdı. Derken bir gün yolu şaşırdı, gece geldi çattı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders jadwa as an "eksi" from the fire in his Turkish translation.
rows.anchor: yahut o ateşten bir eksi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul will taste death, wherever and whoever it may be; all will then be resurrected and brought before God for reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: Her nefis her nasıl olsa ve her nerede bulunsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people cannot escape the return to God by fleeing, they should worship no one else and strive to meet Him sincerely and freely, even under coercion.
rows.anchor: huzûr-ı Hakk’a kemâl-i ihlâs ve hürriyet ile gitmeye çalışmalı

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: The transmitted account identifies Luqman as son of Baʿura, from Aazar's descendants, related to Job as a cousin, long-lived and a contemporary of David from whom he learned.
rows.anchor: Lokman b. Bâ‘ûrâ ki Âzer evlâdından olup Eyyûb aleyhisselâm’ın hemşire veya teyzezâdesi imiş

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: The account says Luqman practiced a craft, may have served as a judge among the Israelites, and issued legal opinions before David's mission.
rows.anchor: Dâvûd aleyhisselâm’a yetişmiş ve ondan ilim ahzetmiş ve onun ba‘sinden evvel iftâ da edermiş

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some held that Luqman was a prophet, but the majority considered him a sage rather than a prophet.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bunun bir nebî olduğuna da kāil olmuşlar ise de cumhûrun kavlince nebî değil bir hakîm idi

rows.speaker: İbn Rüşd
rows.claim: Ibn Rushd's distinction is that every prophet is a sage, but not every sage is a prophet.
rows.anchor: İbn Rüşd’ün Tehâfüt’ünde dediği gibi her nebî hakîm ise de her hakîm nebî değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scholarly definition of wisdom is a perfected human faculty for acquiring theoretical knowledge and acting virtuously to the extent of one's capacity.
rows.anchor: nefs-i insânînin nazarî ilimleri iktibas ve ameliyyâtta ef‘âl-i fâzılaya tâkati nisbetinde tam bir meleke iktisab ederek tekemmül etmesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its full sense, wisdom coordinates knowledge and action so action reaches its aim through knowing causes and reasons.
rows.anchor: ilel ü esbâbı bilerek gayeye isabet edecek vechile ameli ilme, ilmi amele tevfik etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is a great divine gift: discerning God's ordering of causes and laws and deriving practical results from it calls for gratitude in knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: hikmetiyle vaz‘u tahsis buyurduğu esbâb ve ahkâmı, yani kanunları keşfederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intellectual gratitude recognizes wisdom as God's gift and declares God free of shirk; practical gratitude seeks God's pleasure rather than one's own desires.
rows.anchor: hikmet Allah teâlâ’nın bir vergisi olduğunu bilerek Allah’ı şirkten tenzih etmektir. Amelî haysiyeti de ef‘âlinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever gives thanks benefits only himself, since the benefit ultimately returns to him.
rows.anchor: Ve her kim şükrederse sırf kendi lehine şükretmiş olur. Çünkü sonunda fâidesi kendine ait olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ungrateful misuse wisdom by attributing creation and achievement to themselves; this harms them, while God has no need and is praiseworthy in Himself.
rows.anchor: o hikmeti Allah’tan bilmeyip “ben yapıyorum, ben yaratıyorum” diyerek şükretmez de sû’-i isti‘mâl ederse kendi aleyhine eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains ḥamīd as either one who praises Himself even if no one else does or one praised implicitly by all creatures.
rows.anchor: Hâmiddir, hiç kimse övmese bile kendini övmesini bilir. Yahud mahmûddur, bütün mahlûkāt O’na lisân-ı hâl ile hamd eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman's counsel to his son provides an example of how he expressed gratitude for wisdom.
rows.anchor: Bu taksimden sonra Lokman’ın şükrünü nasıl edâ ettiğine dair hikmet ve ahlâktan bir iki numûne zikrolunarak

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib defines waʿẓ as a deterrent accompanied by warning or fear.
rows.anchor: Râgıb’ın beyânına göre “va‘z”

rows.speaker: İmam Halil
rows.claim: Khalil defines waʿẓ as recalling good in a way that softens the heart; Elmalılı judges this definition better.
rows.anchor: İmam Halil ise kalbi inceltecek vechile hayrı hatırlatmak demiştir ki daha güzeldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is injustice because it gives God's due to another and places worship outside its proper place.
rows.anchor: Çünkü zulüm bir şeyi mevzi‘inin gayriye koymaktır. Allah’ın hakkını Allah’tan başkasına vermektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk also degrades the human soul, which God honored, by making it worship a created being.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın mükerrem kıldığı, şeref verdiği nefs-i insânîyi mahlûka ibadet ettirerek tezlil eylemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is an especially grave injustice because no one besides God can ever rightly or possibly occupy the status of deity; unlike property, divine status cannot be transferred.
rows.anchor: mâbudluğu Allah’ın mâsivâsına vermektir. Allah’ın mâsivâsının ise mâbud olmasına hiçbir vechile cevaz ve imkân yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical command to honor parents is a standalone divine statement inserted while recounting Luqman's counsel, reinforcing the ban on shirk.
rows.anchor: istıtrad suretiyle mu‘teriza hâlinde başlı başına bir kelâm-ı ilâhîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse, or at least its second verse, was reportedly revealed about Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother.
rows.anchor: Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkās radıyallâhu anh ile anası hakkında nâzil olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports that Saʿd refused to leave Islam when his mother threatened to starve herself; she eventually ate.
rows.anchor: yapma ana, ben bu dini hiçbir şey için terk etmem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahn ʿalā wahn is a circumstantial description of the mother; wahn means weakness in movement, increasing weakness upon weakness.
rows.anchor: Vehn, vehn üstüne bu terkîb-i vasfî “ümm”den hâldir. “Vehn” harekette za‘ftır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of weaning in two years sets the maximum nursing period at two years, as held by the two Imams and al-Shafiʿi.
rows.anchor: süt kesimi de iki yılda bunun zâhirinden emzik müddetinin a‘zamîsi

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa instead held a thirty-month nursing period as a precaution, using 46:15, though the fatwa follows the two Imams.
rows.anchor: Lakin İmâm-ı A‘zam ihtiyat olmak üzere Sûre-i Ahkāf’ta gelecek olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Abu Hanifa held thirty months, the fatwa follows the position of the two Imams.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh fetvâ İmâmeyn kavlinedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase "that you give thanks" explains the instruction to humanity: God enjoined gratitude to Him and to one's parents.
rows.anchor: Şükret diye bununla وَوَصَّيْنَا tefsir olunuyor. Yani şöyle: Diye tavsiye ettik ki şükret

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: When asked whom one should treat well, the Prophet answered: one's mother three times, then one's father.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’a “ben kime iyilik edeyim?” diye sormuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude to parents means honoring their rights through obedience, kindness, service, and prayer; the topic is also explained in Surat al-Isra.
rows.anchor: Anaya babaya şükür, haklarını gözeterek itaat ve ihsanda bulunmak ve dua etmektir. Sûre-i İsrâ’da bilhassa beyan buyurulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the return is to God, He will question people about whether they gave thanks.
rows.anchor: Dönüş ise Banadır. Yani şükredip etmediğinizi o vakit Ben sorarım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer disciplines and perfects the self, while enjoining right and forbidding wrong guide others toward perfection and lead society rightly.
rows.anchor: Yavrum, namazı devamlı kıl kendini erdirmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong is difficult and may bring afflictions, so one must patiently endure what follows.
rows.anchor: yani emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’l-münker yapmak kolay değildir

rows.speaker: Umeyr b. Habîb
rows.claim: Umayr advised his sons to prepare for harm before commanding right and forbidding wrong, and to be certain of God's reward; certainty makes suffering feel lighter.
rows.anchor: Herhangi biriniz emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’l-münker yapmak isterse ondan evvel ezâya hazırlansın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These acts are among the weighty matters that require resolve.
rows.anchor: Çünkü bu işlerin her birisi azmolunacak büyük işlerdendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amāna derives as a verbal noun from the root of security and trustworthiness, and came also to name what is entrusted; it is broader than a deposit, with the first sense fitting this verse better.
rows.anchor: “Emânet” aslında “mîm”in zammıyla أمن يأمن’den masdar olup eminlik, yani âharın hukūku emniyet edilip inanılabilir

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most exegetes interpret the trust as religious obligations or duties.
rows.anchor: Ekseriyetle müfessirîn bunu teklif veya ferâiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust is voluntary vicegerency: carrying out God's commands and prohibitions concerning His and people's rights, unlike the compelled obedience of other things.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın gerek kendi hukūkuna ve gerek halkın hukūkuna müte‘allik emr ü nehyinin, ahkâmının icrâsına Allah’ın emîni

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth accepted God's creational command willingly, as in 41:11, but balked when asked to carry the trust concerning others' rights.
rows.anchor: öyle iken âharın hukūkunu yüklenmek mânasını ifade eden emanet kendilerine arz olunduğu zaman çekindiler

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the offer and refusal literally; many instead see a representative metaphor picturing the trust's immense weight.
rows.anchor: çokları emânetin azametini beyan için isti‘âre-i temsîliye suretinde bir tasvir olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfilling the trust brings great honor, while failing to fulfill it brings betrayal, liability, and disgrace.
rows.anchor: Emânet îfâ edildiği takdirde neticesi çok büyük bir keramet olduğu gibi, îfâ edilemediği takdirde de hıyânet ve garâmetle büyük bir rüsvâlıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity accepted the trust and vicegerency, but "very unjust, very ignorant" describes the human kind rather than every individual.
rows.anchor: O insan cidden zalûm cehûl bulunuyor her ferdi değil, insan cinsi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is unjust by neglecting God's and other people's rights and thereby wronging himself; ignorant because he does not grasp the outcome of his choice.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın ve ibâdullahın hukūkunu yüklendiği hâlde lâyıkıyla îfâ etmeyip kendine yazık ediyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust's consequence is punishment for male and female hypocrites and polytheists who betray it, and acceptance of repentance and mercy for believing men and women who try to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: Allah, âkıbette münafıkların erkeğine dişisine ve müşriklerin erkeğine dişisine azab edecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If hypocrites and polytheists repent and believe, God too accepts their repentance and forgives them.
rows.anchor: Münafıklar, müşrikler de tevbe edip imana gelirlerse onların da tevbelerini kabul edip mağfiret eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who fulfill the trust attain the greatest triumph and the vision of God; the blessing deserves praise and gratitude.
rows.anchor: büyük fevze ermiş, Dîdâr-ı ilâhîye kavuşmuş olacaklardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links this conclusion to the beauty of the next surah, Saba, beginning with praise of God.
rows.anchor: bundan sonra Sûre-i Sebe’in de اَلْحَمْدُ للهِِّٰ ile başlaması ne güzeldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The finest speech is the call to God joined with righteous action and an open profession of belonging to the Muslims; this answers the disbelievers' claim that their hearts are veiled.
rows.anchor: kâfirlerin sözlerine karşı ne güzel bir cevaptır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling to God is the way of prophets and their heirs; as 12:108 says, it includes the Prophet and those who follow him and call with insight.
rows.anchor: Allah’a davet enbiyânın ve verese-i enbiyâ olan ermişlerin mesleğidir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas says this verse was revealed concerning the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bir rivayette bunun Resûlullah hakkında

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas says it was revealed concerning the Prophet's Companions.
rows.anchor: bir rivayette de ashâbı hakkında nâzil olduğu nakledilmiş

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha reportedly said the verse was revealed concerning callers to prayer.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe’den de müezzinler hakkında nâzil olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the surah is Meccan and the call to prayer was instituted in Medina, the report about muezzins means the verse's teaching also applies to them; the adhan is among the finest speech.
rows.anchor: Sûre Mekkî olmak, ezan ise Medîne’de meşrû kılınmış bulunmak hasebiyle müezzinler hakkında nüzûlü rivayetini hükmün onlara da şümûlü mânasına anlamak iktizâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling to God includes calling believers to practice, not only calling unbelievers to faith; it means inviting people to monotheism and obedience, ultimately to meeting God.
rows.anchor: mü’minleri amele davet de bu mânada dâhildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A true caller's words cannot remain empty: the caller must reform himself, embody divine character, and let good deeds attest to his message.
rows.anchor: o davet yalnız kuru bir laftan ibaret kalmamalı, hâli kāline muhalif olmamalı, amel-i sâlihe iktiran etmelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller must be a sincere Muslim, free of shirk and steadfast in saying that God is Lord; without Islam, action is not fully righteous and is not truly a call to God.
rows.anchor: Birisi de İslâm’dır, dâ‘î müslimînden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling with insight and, when required, taking up the sword are included among righteous actions.
rows.anchor: basiret üzere bulunmak ve îcâbında seyfe sarılmak bu amel-i sâlih cümlesindendir

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reports Zayd ibn Ali's statement that he called to God by the sword, likely driving him to revolt against Umayyad tyrants; Elmalılı praises Zayd's learning and his recorded exegetical discussions with his brother Muhammad al-Baqir.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân Bahr’da der ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good and evil are not equal, and neither are all good acts or all evil acts; their effects and degrees vary.
rows.anchor: her hasene de bir olmaz, her seyyie de; hem güzel huyların, iyi amellerin âsâr ve ahkâmda mertebeleri muhteliftir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When inviting to God, one should avoid intensifying wrongdoing and repel evil with the best treatment or the finest form of the call to God.
rows.anchor: Emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’lmünker ile Allah’a davet yapılırken kötülüklerin teşdîdine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best way to counter evil is the call to God joined to righteous action, especially answering wrongdoing with kindness, which is better than mere pardon or patience.
rows.anchor: amel-i sâlihin en güzeli de kötülüğe karşı iyiliktir ki mücerred aftan, sabırdan daha güzeldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites Abu Sufyan as an example of an enemy becoming a close, compassionate ally.
rows.anchor: Denilmiştir ki nitekim Ebû Süfyan öyle oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those who cultivate patience can attain the disposition of repelling evil with the best response, since true patience restrains revenge.
rows.anchor: kötülüğü en güzel hasene ile def‘etmek seciyesine ancak sabredenler, sabrı huy edinenler erdirilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This disposition is reached only by someone with a great spiritual share, a high soul and virtue, and a large gift from God.
rows.anchor: kuvve-i rûhiyye ve fezâil-i nefsiyeden yüksek bir derece ile, ni‘met-i ilâhiyeden büyük bir nasîbe mazhar olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Satan provokes someone, they should refuse to follow and seek God's protection; God hears the refuge-seeking and knows the person's intention and state.
rows.anchor: Senin sığınmanı işitir, niyetini ve her hâlini bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are signs of God's existence, power, knowledge, and wisdom; their changes show that the world is not static and point to its Creator and to an afterlife.
rows.anchor: bunlar gösterir ki yukarıda yaratıldıkları beyan olunan Arz ve semâsı ile bu âlem bir kararda, bir tabiatta durup kalmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of night and day warns the arrogant and consoles those in grief.
rows.anchor: gece ile gündüzün bu ihtârında mağrurlara bir inzar, mağmumlara bir tesliyet mündemicdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering of night/day before sun/moon preserves the sun's link to daytime, signals its precedence over the moon, evokes the transition from day to night, and balances the paired sounds.
rows.anchor: Leyl ü nehâra nazaran Şems ü Kamer’in aksedilerek ifade edilmesinde birkaç fâide vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are created signs and ornaments of the lower heaven, so they must not be worshiped; prostration belongs to their Creator and is the most specific form of worship.
rows.anchor: ne Şems’e ne de Kamer’e secde etmeyin çünkü onlar da sizin gibi mahluklardır

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says the feminine plural pronoun in khalaqahunna refers to the four signs: night, day, sun, and moon.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî’nin beyânına göre âyât teviliyle leyl ü nehar ve Şems ü Kamer’e râci‘olmak üzere cem‘-i müennes getirilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may also include all the stars together with the sun and moon, as in the statements that all swim in an orbit.
rows.anchor: Şems ü Kamer’le beraber bütün nücûma dahi ircâ‘ı melhuzdur

rows.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi places the prostration at the end of the first verse, at the word taʿbudun.
rows.anchor: İmam Şâfiî’ye göre secde işbu تَعْبُدُونَ’da yapılır

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanife
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa places the prostration at the end of the next verse, la yas'amun, because the discourse is complete there; Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Abu Wa'il, and Bakr ibn Abdullah agree, with similar reports from five Successors.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanife Hazretleri’ne göre ikinci âyetin nihâyetinde لَا يَسْـَٔمُونَ’da yapılmalıdır. Çünkü kelâm orada tamam oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dry earth is portrayed as a humbled person with a bowed neck; the comparison warns the arrogant and signals that the humble will rise.
rows.anchor: Arz’ın hüsran ve kuraklık hâlindeki perişanlığı zillete düşmüş bir kimsenin boynunu büktüğü huşû‘, yani tezellül hâline benzetilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain makes the earth stir and swell; the One who revives it can revive the dead and has power over everything, so believers should persist in calling to God.
rows.anchor: elbette ölüleri dirilticidir. Rûhsuz cesedlere rûh verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dharw means scattering, carrying off as dust, or breaking into fragments; dhariyat can include winds, volcanic eruptions, angels spreading creatures, and later or future explosive forces.
rows.anchor: “Zerv” tozutup götürmek, savurmak, kırıp ufalamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites Baydawi's broad gloss about causes that scatter creatures, contrasting it with the majority's narrower identification with winds.
rows.anchor: bu umûmu göstermiştir. Ekser müfessirînin

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Most exegetes restrict dhariyat to winds based on a report from Ali; Elmalılı treats this as an example rather than an exhaustive definition.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin “riyâh” ile iktifâ etmesi Hazret-i Ali’den vârid olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can also be understood as women who bear many children and spread progeny.
rows.anchor: mefhum itibariyle zürriyet neşreden velûd kadınlar diye de mâna verilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones carrying a burden may be rain-bearing clouds, winds bearing clouds, pregnant women, or their causes; they may be the same forces as before or different ones.
rows.anchor: yağmur yüklenen bulutlar, bulutları taşıyan rüzgârlar veya gebe kadınlar veya bütün bunların sebepleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things that sail smoothly may be ships and comparable means such as trains and automobiles.
rows.anchor: gemiler ve emsâli trenler, otomobiller gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apportioners of a command are angels distributing God's orders to direct what is carried to its destination, including Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and Azrael; the oath recalls their service at judgment.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın emrini taksim ve tevzî‘eden melâikeye; Cebrâil, Mîkâil, İsrâfil, Azrâil gibi emir meleklerine kasem olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people are promised—including new creation, resurrection, emergence, entry into the next life, and abiding—is certainly true.
rows.anchor: ba‘s ü hurûc, duhûl ü hulûd hep doğrudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The din will certainly occur: people are accountable and will receive reward for good and punishment for evil, each finding what they did.
rows.anchor: Ve muhakkak ki cezâ şüphesiz vâki‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hubuk may be the plural of habika or hibak; Elmalılı gives tariqa/turuq and mithal/muthul as comparable plural forms.
rows.anchor: “Tarîka” “turuk”, “misâl” “müsül” gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habika is carefully and firmly woven patterned fabric.
rows.anchor: “Habîke” dikkat ve itina ile sağlam sanatlı dokunmuş yol yol hâreli güzel kumaşa denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hibak describes the ripples in sea or sand made by a gentle breeze, as well as waves in tightly curled hair.
rows.anchor: “Hibâk” da rüzgâr lâtif estiği zaman denizde veya kumda husûle gelen yol yol kırıntılara denir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root habk means binding firmly and making a tight, strong, artfully patterned weave; the essence is durable, beautiful weaving.
rows.anchor: Maddenin aslı olan “habk” sıkı bağlayıp muhkem kılmak ve kumaşı sıkı sağlam

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: Many exegetes understand hubuk as the sky's patterned or striped paths.
rows.anchor: Çokları hâreli, yollu yollu mânasıyla zâtü’t-tarâik diye tefsir etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some understand the paths as star routes, intellectual ways leading to knowledge of the Creator, or the Milky Way.
rows.anchor: Bundan da bazıları yıldızların mahrekleri mânasına mahsüs yolları

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Ikrima, Mujahid, and Rabi are reported to gloss hubuk as a beautiful, well-proportioned creation.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas, Katâde, İkrime, Mücâhid ve Rebî‘’den rivayet olunduğuna göre de ذَاتُ الْخَلْقِ الْمُسْتَوِي الْجَي ِّدِ güzel düzgün hilkatlı

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Another report from Mujahid glosses hubuk as strong construction.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den diğer bir rivayette de مَتِينُ الْبـُنـْيَانِ diye tefsir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı synthesizes these meanings as a finely woven, firm, patterned heaven whose harmony points to the Creator's unity and power and rebukes those who disagree about God.
rows.anchor: yıldızları ve türlü türlü medâr ve mahrekleri ile pek sıkı ve gayet sanatlı bir surette dokunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word combines paths with strong, beautiful weaving, suggesting a unified whole that brings multiplicity together; the general heaven is more likely than only the seventh heaven.
rows.anchor: “Habk” maddesi hem yolları hem de sağlam ve güzel bir dokuma mânasını mutazammın olmak itibariyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' speech is internally inconsistent: they acknowledge the Creator yet worship other gods, disagree over idols and aims, contradict one another about the Prophet, and deny judgment while hoping idols intercede.
rows.anchor: Gökleri ve yeri yaratan Allah dersiniz, sonra da tutar başkalarına taparsınız, muhtelif mâbudlara taptığınız için mezhebleriniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about being turned away can mean that those destined to turn from conflicting speech return to the truth and believe.
rows.anchor: O muhtelif kavilden dönmesi mukadder olan döner, doğruya iman eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, those already diverted from the path and habituated to error are driven away from belief in the true promise and judgment into conflicting speech.
rows.anchor: yahut hak yolundan saptırılmış, sapıklık da tabiatı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned guessers are liars who assert mere conjecture and their own desires in the name of thought.
rows.anchor: zann u tahminlerine göre atan, fikir nâmına kendi hevâlarını ileri süren yalancılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless inside an engulfing torrent-like swamp, stupor, drunkenness, or ignorance, unaware of God and the disaster coming to them.
rows.anchor: müstevlî bir sel gibi kendilerini her noktadan sarıp bürümüş olan bir batak, bir sarhoşluk veya bir cehalet içinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask when the Judgment Day is mockingly because they do not believe.
rows.anchor: “O din günü, yani vâki‘olacağı haber verilen o cezânın günü ne vakit?” diye soruyorlar. İnanmadıkları için eğlenmek istiyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their answer is that the day they will be tormented over the Fire will come.
rows.anchor: Onların ateş üzerinde kıvrandırılacakları gün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna originally meant exposing gold or silver ore to fire to separate the good from the bad; by extension it means trial, testing, seduction, or infatuation, and here means punishment or the unbelief and corruption that cause it.
rows.anchor: Altın ve gümüş herhangi bir cevheri iyisini kötüsünden ayırmak için ateşe arzetmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing will be in gardens and springs beyond human measure, receiving what their Lord gives with welcome and contentment.
rows.anchor: Rablerinin kendilerine verdiğini alarak yani hüsn-i kabul ile telakkī edip râzı ve hoşnut olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They receive this reward because they were beneficent in worldly life, doing good deeds well and thereby deserving recompense; this shows taqwa has a positive dimension of good action as well as avoidance.
rows.anchor: Güzel ameller yapar ve güzel yaparlardı, onun için ecr ü mükâfâta müstahik olmuşlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They slept little at night, acting on 73:2; love of God and concern for the afterlife kept them awake in worship and duty.
rows.anchor: Allah şevki, âhiret endişesiyle gözlerine uyku girmez, ibadet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hujuʿ means little sleep, especially sleep at night; mā can be extra, relative, or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: az uyku ve bilhassa gece uykusu. ما mezîd veya mevsul veya masdariyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā is negative, the verse can mean they never slept even briefly on some nights; another report divides it into two clauses, but the apparent reading is that they slept little.
rows.anchor: Bir rivayette de az idiler geceden uyumazlardı diye iki cümle olarak mâna verilmişse de zâhir olan evvelkidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite worshiping at night, they sought forgiveness at dawn as though they had spent the night in sin; dawn is the finest time for accepted prayer and supplication.
rows.anchor: Ve seher vakitleri onlar istiğfar ederlerdi yani geceleri öyle ibadet etmekle beraber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A restrictive pronoun emphasizes that these beneficent people are the ones who make the especially acceptable dawn supplication for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: Yani dua ve istiğfârın en güzel vakti olan o seher vakitleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The asker is someone who begs; the deprived person is needy but self-restrained and mistaken for wealthy, so even charity passes them by.
rows.anchor: “Sâil” isteyen, dilenen; “mahrûm” ta‘affüfünden dolayı zengin zannedildiği için sadakadan dahi mahrum bulunan muhtaç

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: The Prophet says a poor person is not merely someone satisfied by one or two meals or a few dates; the poor person cannot find enough and is not recognized to receive charity.
rows.anchor: Odur ki bulamaz ve bilinip kendisine sadaka da verilemez

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the deprived as an unfortunate person unable to earn.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bir rivayette

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Others define the deprived as someone whose means seemed near but then moved away; Elmalılı prefers the broader first interpretation.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da, rızık esbâbı kendisine

rows.speaker: Kādî Münzir b. Sa‘îd
rows.claim: Because "right" apparently signals an obligation, Qadi Mundhir ibn Saʿid held that the right for the asker and deprived is obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: Kādî Münzir b. Sa‘îd bunun farz olan zekât olduğuna kāil olmuştur

rows.speaker: çokları
rows.claim: Many interpret it as voluntary charity because the surah is Meccan while zakat became obligatory in Medina, or as a generous pledged share in addition to zakat.
rows.anchor: çokları bunu tetavvu‘a hamletmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This care for the needy is especially important to the rise of the Muslim community.
rows.anchor: İslâm cemaatinin yükselmesinde çok büyük ehemmiyeti olan bu noktanın bilhassa câlib-i dikkat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs in the earth and people's selves show that judgment and accountability are real; history reveals differing outcomes for the righteous and corrupt, believers and deniers, while human life displays God's power and duty.
rows.anchor: cezânın ve mes’ûliyetin vâki‘ve dinin hak olduğunu gösterirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision in heaven means causes such as rain and heat, while the promised things may include all promises and threats or may specifically mean reward.
rows.anchor: Semâda da rızkınız yağmur, harâret vesâire gibi esbâbı

rows.speaker: ekseriyet
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand the promised thing as reward and report that Paradise lies above the seventh heaven, beneath the Throne.
rows.anchor: ekseriyetle sevab ile tefsir etmişler ve cennet yedinci semânın üstünde, Arş’ın tahtında olduğunu nakl eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of accountability and recompense is as certain as the fact that people speak.
rows.anchor: sizin nâtıkıyetiniz nasıl muhakkak bir emr-i vâki‘ise mes’ûliyetiniz, vaad olunan cezâ ve mükâfâtınız da öylece vâki‘olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction suppresses the verb governing "the heaven" and explains it through the attached pronoun in "we built it"; this wording expresses inference from the created effect to its Maker.
rows.anchor: Eserden müessire istidlâli ifade eden bu üslupta lafız mânanın mazmûnuna terkîbi ile de intibak etmiştir
